title: Hiring a Brother-in-Law's Bakery
scenario: Ximena Cortés manages facilities for a regional hospital network in Bogotá and must choose a catering vendor for staff cafeterias. The best technical bid comes from a bakery-restaurant owned by her husband's brother, who has never done work at this scale but has solid references. Two other bidders are slightly more expensive and have long track records. Hospital policy requires disclosure of family ties but does not forbid awarding the contract to relatives. The family has recently been strained by money problems, and this contract would help. The decision is due at Friday's procurement meeting.
options: Disclose the relationship and recuse herself, letting a colleague choose among the bids without her input.
Disclose the relationship but remain on the panel, scoring all bids with a written rationale for the committee to review.
Choose one of the established bidders and say nothing about the family tie, to avoid any appearance of favouritism.

title: The Advisor Who Owns the Fund
scenario: Abdulrahman Al-Farsi is an independent financial advisor in Muscat serving retired teachers. He has discovered a new equity fund with solid fundamentals that suits several clients, but the fund's management company has quietly offered him a placement fee of two percent, which he is not required to disclose under current local rules. The fee is higher than the alternatives pay, which are comparable in quality. His practice is small and struggling after losing two clients. Recommending the fund could secure his income, while an alternative may serve clients marginally better after fees.
options: Recommend the best-matching fund for each client regardless of fees and decline the placement fee.
Recommend the fund, and clearly disclose the placement fee to each client in writing so they can decide.
Recommend the fund without disclosing the fee, reasoning that it is legal and that the fund is genuinely suitable.

title: Reviewing a Rival's Grant Proposal
scenario: Professor Ingeborg Lindqvist sits on a Swedish research council panel assessing applications for a major biotechnology grant. One proposal comes from a lab led by a former doctoral student of hers, with whom she remains close, and another from a group that is directly competing with her own funded project. Panel rules require declaring conflicts, but the panel is small and few experts can assess this field. If she steps aside, the panel may lack the knowledge to judge both fairly. Reviews are due in six days and are confidential.
options: Declare both conflicts and step back from the assessments, accepting the panel will have less expertise.
Declare both conflicts but offer written technical comments the panel can weigh as it sees fit.
Declare only the competing-project conflict, treating the relationship with her former student as acceptable collegiality.

title: A Board Seat and a Supplier Deal
scenario: Kofi Mensah-Adjei is chief executive of a mid-sized cocoa processing company in Kumasi. A supplier who is also a close friend invites him to join the supplier's board with a modest annual fee, noting that it will strengthen the commercial relationship. Kofi's company buys a large share of the supplier's output at competitive prices. His own board has no formal rule about outside directorships. Accepting could give him insight into market trends useful to both firms, and he believes he can remain objective. Declining may strain a friendship, and the supplier is financially fragile.
options: Decline the seat to keep his dealings with the supplier clearly arm's length.
Accept the seat only after full disclosure to his own board and with a rule that he abstains on any contract between the firms.
Accept the seat and handle the contract negotiations through a deputy without formally notifying the board.

title: The Doctor and the Device Rep's Free Course
scenario: Dr. Marcelo Bianchi is head of orthopaedics at a public hospital in Milan and is invited by an implant manufacturer to give paid lectures at an annual conference in Dubai, with travel and accommodation covered. The manufacturer's products are among those he uses, and the hospital is choosing between suppliers next quarter. The lectures would also give junior colleagues exposure, as he may bring two of them. He believes the implants are among the best available. National rules require reporting such invitations to the hospital's ethics office, which sometimes withholds approval.
options: Decline the invitation until the hospital's supplier choice has been made, to avoid any link between the two.
Report the invitation, accept only with ethics-office approval, and recuse himself from the supplier decision.
Accept and report it later, since his clinical choice is based on evidence and the conference benefits his juniors.
tension: benefit to juniors vs. appearance of bias

title: Naming the Contractor Who Lent the Truck
scenario: Sipho Dlamini is a municipal roads supervisor in a rural district of Eswatini. During flooding, a private contractor lent a truck and driver at no charge to clear a blocked bridge, saving residents days of isolation. The contractor is now bidding on a road resurfacing tender that Sipho helps evaluate. His evaluation scores will carry weight, and the contractor's bid is reasonable but not the cheapest. Residents spoke warmly of the contractor's help. Sipho feels indebted, and the municipality has few other competent firms in the area.
options: Disclose the favour, recuse himself from the evaluation, and let others score the tender.
Stay on the evaluation, applying published criteria strictly and recording that he disclosed the favour to his superior.
Score the bids as usual without mention, regarding the flood help as a separate act of community goodwill.

title: Consulting for the Competitor on Weekends
scenario: Yuki Tanabe is a product designer at a Kyoto toy company. A start-up in Osaka offers her paid freelance work on weekends designing wooden puzzles, a market her employer is considering entering. Her employment contract forbids outside work in the same industry without approval, yet approval is rarely granted. She has money worries because of caring for her parents, and the start-up is too small to compete with her employer today. She has access to her employer's unreleased designs and could easily avoid using them.
options: Decline the freelance offer and look for other income outside the toy industry.
Ask her employer for formal permission and disclose what she knows about the start-up's plans.
Take the freelance work discreetly, taking care to keep it separate from her employer's confidential material.
tension: family financial need vs. contractual loyalty

title: A Judge's Spouse and the Zoning Case
scenario: Magistrate Tendai Moyo hears planning disputes in Harare. A case arrives involving a developer who has recently employed her husband as a consultant on an unrelated project, a fact few know. The case is routine, and the law is clear. Only two magistrates are available in the district, and the other has a backlog of eight months. Recusal would delay residents who wait to learn if the development can proceed. Judicial rules require recusal in cases of reasonable apprehension of bias, but the standard is open to interpretation.
options: Recuse herself and refer the case to the other magistrate, accepting the delay for residents.
Disclose the husband's consultancy openly to all parties and proceed only if no one objects.
Hear the case without disclosure, trusting that the clarity of the law makes the link immaterial.
tension: justice delayed vs. appearance of bias

title: The Investor Relations Lead's Shares
scenario: Oluwaseun Bello-Hart works in investor relations for a UK-listed renewable energy firm. Before an announcement of a delayed project, which will likely reduce the share price, she holds a large block of shares she received as part of her pay, and she is due to pay for her mother's surgery next month. Trading rules close her window two weeks before announcements, but a clause allows exceptions for financial hardship with the compliance officer's approval. The compliance officer is her friend. She is unsure whether the clause was meant for such situations.
options: Wait for the trading window to reopen and arrange a loan for the surgery instead, even at a higher cost.
Apply for the hardship exception, disclosing the pending announcement to the compliance officer, and abide by their decision.
Sell a portion of shares now, justified by the surgery, without seeking approval given the urgency.

title: Referring Patients to My Own Clinic
scenario: Dr. Sunita Rao is a general practitioner in Pune employed by a large public health scheme. She also owns a share in a private physiotherapy centre nearby, which offers shorter waiting times than public services. Some patients with back pain would benefit from quick treatment, but public physiotherapy has a three-month wait. The scheme does not prohibit referrals but expects staff to declare interests, which she has not done because she feared complications. Patients often cannot afford private fees, though her centre offers small discounts.
options: Declare her ownership to the scheme and refer patients to the centre only with transparent patient consent and the discount.
Refer patients only to the public service to avoid any suspicion that she profits from her referrals.
Continue referring patients who prefer faster care, without declaring the ownership, because the clinical benefit is real.

title: Choosing the Architect for a Mosque Extension
scenario: Hassan El-Amrani chairs the building committee of a community mosque in Casablanca, funded by donations. The committee must choose an architect for the extension. His cousin's firm submitted a good, mid-priced design, while a more famous firm submitted a better design at a higher price that would absorb nearly all the budget. Committee members know Hassan's relationship to the first firm and look to him to lead. He is trusted for his integrity but is conscious that donors may be sceptical. The decision must be made before Ramadan starts.
options: Step down from the decision, ask the committee to choose without him, and abide by their result.
Remain in the room, state his relationship plainly, and ask the committee to vote openly on each firm.
Argue for his cousin's firm as the most prudent use of donations, since the budget is limited.

title: The Journalist Dating the Politician's Aide
scenario: Aino Virtanen, a political reporter at a Helsinki daily, has begun a relationship with an aide to a cabinet minister. Her newsroom has no rule for this. She is currently investigating a procurement scandal touching the minister's department, and her editor has not been told. Her work is considered fair, and the story is important. Disclosing the relationship might remove her from the beat, delaying the story, while hiding it risks accusations of bias if it becomes known. She has not received any confidential information from her partner, whom she keeps out of her work.
options: Tell her editor about the relationship now and accept being reassigned from the story.
Tell her editor and propose staying on the story with extra editing oversight and a note to readers.
Say nothing, since she maintains a strict separation and the public interest in the story is high.
tension: public interest vs. appearance of bias

title: Selling the Land to the School Board I Sit On
scenario: Rosalind Achterberg is a trustee of an independent school in Cape Town. A parcel of land she co-owns with her sister lies next to the school and would be ideal for a new sports field. The trustees have been looking for such land for years, and she knows that the asking price she and her sister would set is fair and slightly below market. Other nearby plots are unsuitable or more expensive. The school's constitution requires trustees to declare interests but doesn't address land sales by trustees explicitly. Other trustees suspect nothing.
options: Decline to sell, preferring to avoid any dealings between herself and the school she serves.
Disclose her interest, leave the discussion, and offer the land at an independently appraised price for the other trustees to decide.
Sell the land at the slightly below-market price without raising the matter, since the school clearly benefits.

title: The Engineer's Side Business in Used Parts
scenario: Tiago Carvalho runs maintenance at a bus operator in Maputo. A relative sells reconditioned engine components, cheaper than new ones. Tiago can approve purchases up to a limit without competitive tender. The relative's parts have lasted well in testing, and using them would cut the company's costs enough to prevent fare increases for commuters. However, he would obtain a modest commission from his relative, which he has not asked for. The company's accountant does not look closely at purchase approvals.
options: Route the purchasing decision through a formal tender and declare his relative's interest to his manager.
Buy from the relative, decline any commission, and tell his manager about the relationship in writing.
Buy from the relative and accept the commission, as the arrangement benefits the company and customers too.

title: Advising Both Sides of a Farm Sale
scenario: Declan Ó Briain is a solicitor in a small town in County Cork. An elderly farmer, long-time client, wants to sell land to his neighbour, who is also a long-time client of Declan. Both ask Declan to handle the paperwork to save money, saying they have agreed on a price. The price looks fair, though the farmer may not realise the land has development potential. The nearest other solicitor is an hour away, and both parties are modest. Professional rules discourage acting for both sides, but allow it with informed consent in limited cases.
options: Act for only one party and ask the other to hire another solicitor, even though it increases their costs.
Act for both with written informed consent, after telling them clearly about the possible conflict and the land's potential value.
Refer both parties elsewhere and decline to act, since the potential conflict is too serious to manage.

title: A Product Reviewer Offered a Stake
scenario: Camille Dubois runs a popular Quebec-based channel reviewing outdoor gear. A young company making camping stoves offers her a small ownership share instead of payment for an honest review, noting that she is free to say whatever she likes. She likes the product but finds a few design flaws. Her audience of about two hundred thousand trusts her independence. Taking the stake could fund her channel, and she believes she could remain fair. Disclosure rules in Canada require her to declare financial ties but do not forbid them.
options: Decline the stake and review the stove independently, or not at all.
Accept the stake, disclose it prominently in the review, and report the flaws plainly.
Accept payment in the standard way as a sponsorship instead of equity, and disclose the sponsorship.

title: My Mentor's Start-up Wants My Vote
scenario: Nguyen Thi Lan sits on an angel-investment committee in Ho Chi Minh City that decides which start-ups receive seed funding. Her former mentor, who helped her launch her career, is pitching a logistics app. The idea is promising but the team is inexperienced. Other committee members do not know of the mentorship. The committee works by consensus, and she is the only member with logistics experience. If she recuses herself, the committee may fund the project without good scrutiny or reject it unfairly. The meeting is tomorrow.
options: Disclose the mentorship, then give her honest technical assessment and let the committee weigh it.
Disclose the mentorship and abstain entirely from the discussion and the vote.
Keep the mentorship private and judge the pitch strictly on its merits, being deliberately harsher to offset any bias.

title: The Procurement Chief's Daughter's Internship
scenario: Arvid Strand heads procurement at a Norwegian offshore services firm. A long-time supplier's director offers an internship to his daughter, who is studying engineering, with a decent salary and good prospects. Nothing was asked in return. Arvid is about to renew that supplier's frame agreement, with a price considered fair. His daughter has struggled to find placements, and he knows the offer reflects her qualifications and not only his position. Company policy forbids accepting gifts above a small value but does not mention benefits to family members.
options: Ask the supplier to withdraw the offer, protecting the integrity of the renewal even at his daughter's expense.
Tell his superior about the offer and let the renewal be handled by another manager while his daughter accepts.
Let his daughter accept the internship independently and proceed with the renewal as planned, without raising it.

title: A Teacher Tutoring Her Own Pupils for Pay
scenario: Mrs. Lakshmi Perera teaches mathematics at a government school in Kandy with a very low salary. Exams at the end of the year determine access to university, and many families pay for private tuition. Parents of three pupils in her class ask her to tutor their children privately for a fee. School regulations discourage but do not prohibit it. She worries that other pupils would feel disadvantaged, but she knows the tutoring would double her income. Several colleagues already do the same quietly, and parents may go to less careful tutors.
options: Refuse to tutor her own pupils and offer free group revision sessions for the whole class instead.
Tutor her pupils privately but disclose it to the principal and ensure she grades exams strictly by marking scheme.
Accept the tutoring quietly, as many colleagues do, and maintain fair grading in class.
tension: common practice vs. conflict of interest

title: Evaluating a Merger My Brother Works For
scenario: Elif Yıldırım works at a competition authority in Ankara and is assigned to evaluate a proposed merger of two pharmacy chains. She then learns her brother is a mid-level manager at one of them, and could lose his job if the merger fails or gain a promotion if it succeeds. The case team is only three people, and her unit is already short of staff. Her superior knows nothing. She is the most experienced economist on the team, and a misjudged merger could raise medicine prices across several provinces.
options: Tell her superior about her brother's role immediately and ask to be removed from the case.
Disclose it and remain on the case in a limited role, with her analysis reviewed independently.
Continue as normal, believing her professional analysis will be unaffected, and mention it only if asked.

title: A Charity Auditor Offered the Gala Table
scenario: Valentina Rossi-Meyer is a freelance auditor in Zurich who audits a well-known conservation charity. The charity's director invites her, free of charge, to a prestigious annual gala, where wealthy donors gather and she could win new clients. The ticket would cost several hundred francs. She suspects the invitation is entirely friendly, since the charity's books are clean. Professional ethics rules require independence in both fact and appearance, but she knows other auditors accept hospitality of this kind. The audit will be signed in three weeks.
options: Decline the invitation or pay for her own ticket, to maintain visible independence during the audit.
Accept the invitation and disclose it to the charity's audit committee as a courtesy.
Accept the invitation without comment, as the books are clean and the hospitality is customary.

title: Choosing Between My Two Employers' Interests
scenario: Folasade Ogunleye works half the week at a state electricity distributor in Abuja and half at a private consultancy that advises solar companies. Her state employer is drafting rules on how rooftop solar can connect to the grid. The consultancy's clients stand to gain from lenient rules, and she is asked to write a technical memo for the state agency. She is among the few engineers who understand the topic. Both employers know of the arrangement, but neither knows the details of her work for the other.
options: Tell the state agency about her consultancy clients and ask to be excused from the memo.
Write the memo under strict disclosure, listing her consultancy relationships and inviting outside review.
Write the memo, drawing a firm line between her two roles and trusting her professional judgement.

title: The Dean's Textbook, Required for All
scenario: Professor Anselmo Gutierrez is dean of engineering at a university in Quito and has written a textbook that is considered one of the best for first-year mechanics. Students must buy it for his department's course, bringing him royalties. Many students struggle with costs, and a free open-source textbook is of slightly lower quality. His colleagues say his book is excellent. There is no university rule on this. Students have started to grumble privately, and a student representative asked him last week whether the requirement is for his own benefit.
options: Donate his royalties from required student sales to a scholarship fund and keep the textbook required.
Stop requiring his textbook and offer the open-source alternative, leaving his book as an optional extra.
Keep the requirement as is, since the book genuinely serves students best and royalties are a normal reward for authorship.

title: Buying From the Cooperative I Helped Found
scenario: Pallavi Deshmukh left a rural women's weaving cooperative in Maharashtra to take a job as sourcing manager at a Mumbai fashion label. She still holds a small ownership share in the cooperative and is proud of what she helped build. Her new employer wants authentic handwoven fabrics, and the cooperative would be an ideal supplier at fair prices. Buying from them would lift incomes of two hundred women. However, she would, as an owner, benefit slightly in dividends. Her employer has not asked about her past affiliations, and there are alternative suppliers of similar quality.
options: Disclose her share to her employer and sell it before any purchases are made, to keep purchasing clean.
Disclose her share to her employer and have a colleague approve every purchase from the cooperative.
Buy from the cooperative without mentioning her share, since the benefit to the women is large and her gain is small.

title: Inspecting the Home Where My Mother Lives
scenario: Gerardus Visser is a health inspector in Utrecht assigned a rotation of care homes for the elderly. His mother has just moved into one of them, which is on his upcoming list. He thinks the home is decent but understaffed, and he knows inspection results influence whether it keeps its licence. If he asks to swap, a colleague with less experience in dementia care would take over. Moving his mother would be traumatic for her. He hasn't mentioned any of this at work, and the inspection is in ten days.
options: Disclose it to his manager and ask for another inspector to take over this home.
Disclose it and carry out the inspection with a second inspector accompanying him.
Carry out the inspection as scheduled, holding himself to the same standards he would apply to any other home.
